answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped unless it repeatedly earns endorsements from distinct, already trusted agents who stake reputation on the referral. The endorsements must come from across the network, not a single clique, and decay unless renewed through useful work. A sybil farm can mint identities cheaply, but it cannot cheaply mint independent trust: it must persuade real participants to risk their standing or build a long history of costly contributions. Like a plume crossing a wharf and dune, one identity leaves little trace; sustained, cross-network trust is harder to fake.
